facts.statement: Allgoviachen fossils date to the Tortonian stage of the Miocene epoch.
This extinct bird genus lived in the Late Miocene at the Hammerschmiede clay pits in Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: Allgoviachen (meaning "Allgäu goose") is an extinct genus of anatid bird from the Late Miocene (Tortonian) Hammerschmiede clay pits of Bavaria, Germany.

facts.statement: The only known species, A. tortonica, is represented by fossil bones from a left leg.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, A. tortonica, known from bones belonging to the left leg.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Hammerschmiede clay pits near Pforzen in the Allgäu region of Bavaria.
facts.quote: The Allgoviachen holotype specimen, SNSB-BSPG 2020 XCIV 1058, was discovered in the Hammerschmiede clay pits of the Allgäu region, near Pforzen, Bavaria, Germany.

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme described the genus and species in 2022.
facts.quote: In 2022, Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme described Allgoviachen tortonica, a new genus and species of antatid, based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Allgäu" for the location and the Greek word for goose.
facts.quote: The generic name, Allgoviachen, combines the Latin "Allgäu", a reference to the type locality, with the Greek "chen," meaning "goose".

facts.statement: Researchers estimated its body mass to be about 2 kg, similar to the Bar-headed goose and Egyptian goose.
facts.quote: The describing authors concluded that Allgoviachen would have had a body size comparable to the extant anserine Anser indicus (Bar-headed goose) and anatine Alopochen aegyptiaca (Egyptian goose), with an estimated body mass of about 2 kg.

facts.statement: Allgoviachen belongs to the family Anatidae.
The species lived between 11.63 and 7.246 million years ago during the Tortonian.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Tortonian (11.63 to 7.246 million years ago)
